messages:
ellen.k: Seeing a spike in gRPC streaming errors for model-inference pods in us-west-2b -> us-west-2c cross-AZ traffic. Token streams are being cut off mid-response and clients hit RPC deadlines.

samir: yup noticed increased p99 latency and a bunch of 'rpc: stream closed' from the gateway logs around 09:12 UTC. Any packet-level indicators?

jia: I pulled tcpdump from a few affected nodes. There's clear packet reordering and bursts of out-of-order segments on the pod network interface (eth0). Example:

```
09:12:17.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 63, id 45823, offset 16384, flags [DF]) 10.0.12.45.54321 > 10.0.34.78.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1457, ack 1, win 501, length 1456
09:12:17.123459 IP 10.0.12.45.54321 > 10.0.34.78.443: Flags [.], seq 1457:2913, ack 1, win 501, length 1456
09:12:17.123457 IP 10.0.12.45.54321 > 10.0.34.78.443: Flags [.], seq 2913:4369, ack 1, win 501, length 1456  # arrives later -> reordering
```

kevin-m: interesting — that pattern is consistent with NIC offloads (GSO/TSO/LRO) + qdisc microbursts or switch re-ordering. Any switch firmware changes?

elllen.k: not that I'm aware of, but oncall-bot shows a capacity rebalancer ran at 09:10 that moved several GPU pods between nodes in the two AZs. Could be coincident.

oncall-bot: rebalancer: moved 12 pods from ip-10-0-12-.* to ip-10-0-34-* at 09:10:02 UTC (reason: binpack evict).

samir: we saw the reorders correlate with network interface counters: rx_nohandler and rx_missed spiking. Run: `ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_|tx_"` showed drops on one host.

jia: Also captured k8s pod logs: model-server reported 'kv-cache miss + regen' followed by long tail token latencies. Streaming paths don't retry tokens so downstream clients see truncated streams.

kevin-m: quick mitigation options: 1) disable GSO/TSO/LRO on affected hosts: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` 2) add txqueuelen bump and ingress policing (qdisc) to smooth microbursts 3) pin critical pods to same AZ / avoid cross-AZ for streaming lanes.

elllen.k: can we flip GSO off on a canary host and observe? Prefer a non-prod GPU pool first.

samir: doing it now on gpu-canary-3 (10.0.12.45). Running `sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` -> will watch tcpdump and app logs.

jia: FYI, Mellanox driver logs show a couple of XSK errors too on the older NICs; firmware v12.3 deployed two months ago. Might be hitting a known reorder bug.

kevin-m: if firmware bug, long-term fix is vendor firmware patch. Short-term: disable offloads, or set `net.core.netdev_max_backlog` higher and tune `netdev_budget` to avoid rx processing stalls. Also consider SR-IOV for heavy streaming pods to reduce kernel path.

elllen.k: results from canary?

samir: after disabling offloads on gpu-canary-3, tcpdump shows much lower reorder. model-server p99 token latency dropped from 220ms -> 42ms and no truncated streams in the last 5m.

jia: rolling same change to two other affected nodes in us-west-2b/2c. Will add a kube affinity rule to keep streaming frontends in-zone until we confirm.

kevin-m: please add a temporary alert to ping infra when packet_reorder_rate > 0.5% for a minute across az pairs; we missed the first spike.

oncall-bot: alert created: infra.packet_reorder_rate (threshold 0.5%, window 60s) -> paging: oncall@sre.team

elllen.k: runbook:
- immediate: disable GSO/TCO/GRO on affected hosts (canary -> roll)
- short: affinity changes to avoid cross-AZ streaming for sensitive models
- medium: vendor engagement for NIC firmware + switch parity check
- long: explore SR-IOV / eBPF XDP bypass for hot paths + testcase that simulates microburst reorder

samir: I'll open a ticket with networking vendor and attach tcpdumps + ethtool stats. Tagging @kevin-m for firmware conversation.

kevin-m: thanks. Also estimate cost impact: the temporary in-zone pinning will increase node count by ~8 GPUs for high-throughput lines; I'll throw numbers into the cost sheet.

elllen.k: ok team, roll forward with the canary -> small roll -> vendor ticket. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
